data.overview:
**DEMO engagement — illustrative as-is map of the UC San Diego Athletics fan and revenue lifecycle.** This is sample data created to demonstrate the application end to end; names, systems, and figures are illustrative.

## What this engagement maps

The path a fan or donor travels: discovering Triton athletics, buying a ticket, attending a game, coming back, and in some cases becoming a season-ticket holder or a Triton Athletic Fund donor. This is the revenue side of the house, and it runs across marketing, ticketing, game-day operations, and development.

The map is drawn against the season just completed. The 2026–27 season is UC San Diego's first in the **West Coast Conference** — new opponents, new travel patterns, and a fresh reason to grow the audience — which is why the unit wanted the as-is picture now rather than after the transition.

## Scope

One person's journey across one season, from **first contact with Triton athletics** through **renewal, lapse, or a first Triton Athletic Fund gift**. Two flagship sports — men's and women's basketball — rather than all 24 programs, so that one venue and one ticketing platform carry the whole map.

The scope deliberately includes the path from ticket buyer to Triton Athletic Fund donor. That is where Athletics meets central Advancement, on gift processing, on deciding who approaches which donor, and on who owns the relationship with a donor who gives to both. Drawing the boundary there makes this a cross-unit map rather than a departmental one.

## The Layer 1 discipline

Layer 1 produces the lifecycle map: a written, agreed account of how the service actually runs — its stages, points of contact, handoffs, decisions, and where it has friction. **It describes the service as it is and proposes no fixes.** Naming AI opportunities is Layer 2's job; only two things carry forward — the list of decisions and the Friction Register.

The six artifacts here are not sequential phases. They are parallel lenses on the same whole service: the **journey map** (the fan's experience) and the **service blueprint** (the operations behind it) share one set of stages and line up stage for stage; the **process documentation** is the detail beneath; the **interview guide** is the shared raw source; the **friction register** logs evidence gathered across all of them; and the **validation packet** integrates the whole and records sign-off.

## Where the work concentrates

Two things, both visible across the map. Relationship data lives in vendor systems that do not talk to each other, so the same person exists as a ticket account, an email contact, a scanned barcode, and a donor record with nothing shared between them. And the person experiences one relationship with the institution while the institution runs it as separate functions.

The handoff from ticket buyer to donor is where the friction is heaviest, because at that point the work changes both systems and units at once.

## The decisions in this service are commercial

Pricing, targeting, outreach timing, and who gets asked to give. There is no protected student record at the centre of this service and no association rulebook governing the calls. What makes the stakes real is different: the standard AI in this territory is largely about **scoring people** — estimating how likely someone is to buy or to give, and sorting people into groups for targeted outreach.

The practice's standing rule is that humans decide about people, money, and ranking. Scoring fans and donors sits directly on that line, so this engagement is where the guardrail gets worked out early, in a comparatively low-stakes setting. The question arrives later regardless, at higher stakes, when advancement and enrollment bring it.

## How AI was used

AI tagged interview notes against a shared label set, drafted first cuts of the journey and blueprint, and grouped related friction — each suggestion shown with the words that prompted it. A person confirmed or rejected every item. One AI output was rejected on principle: a proposed ranking of season-ticket holders by likelihood to give. Ranking people to decide who gets asked for money is a human call under the standing rule, and the log records it that way. See the AI decision log on the Validation screen.

## Where this engagement stands

Mapping is under way, not finished. Artifacts 01–05 are confirmed; the validation packet is in review with one item still contested — who owns the relationship with a donor who gives to both Athletics and a campus unit — and neither the lifecycle owner nor the practice lead has signed off.
